hypotheses.justification: This equality follows from the type of `rule` and the other arguments. In `LocalRule`, the only constructor compatible with source `(∅, Rcond, none)` is `oneSidedR`: `oneSidedL` would require an empty one-sided precondition, ruled out by `OneSidedLocalRule.precond_ne_nil`; the contradiction and loaded constructors have incompatible indices. Matching the result index with `ress_1` and `YS_def` identifies the constructor’s result data, and `OneSidedLocalRule` values with the same precondition are subsingleton (`oneSidedLocalRuleSubsingleton`). Thus `def_rule` can be derived and deleted. These index arguments also cover empty finsets; there is no degenerate constructor exception.
